To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EF-induced PMA reduction is very efficient but EF switching of PMA MTJs is difficult due to the absence of STT effect and large switching uncertainty.
(1) the PMA reduction is not sufficient for EF switching and (2) the EF switching can be realized by the Oersted field-guided approach, but it needs further optimization.

the EF-induced switching of the perpendicular MTJs is very promising for next-generation non-volatile memory applications, and that the key to the success lies in the engineering of materials and MTJ stacks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding of the EF-induced PMA reduction and the EF switching of MTJs with PMA.
the development of a new approach to realize EF switching in MRAMS and the study of the underlying physics of the EF effect in MTJs.
the EF effect on the PMA of CoFeB/Mgo MTJs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PMA reduction by EF is a promising method to realize the sub-20 nm STT-MRAM.
the PMA reduction by EF alone is insufficient to realize the EF switching.
the EF-MRAM technology is very promising and will be realized in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EF switching of PMA MTJs can be achieved at an EF of about 0.5 V/nm with the thermal stability of 50 and the write energy of 1 fJ.
the EF effect can be a key enabler for future MRAMs with PMA and is worth further investigation.
the EF switching can be realized in MTJs with high PMA, but the EF switching is not efficient enough to compete with STT switching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Oersted field assisted EF-MRAM is the most promising approach for future MRAM development.
the EF effect can be utilized to realize the bidirectional switching in MRAM cells by combining the Oersted field and STT effects, which is very promising for the development of future MRAMs.
the PMA reduction by EF is not sufficient for the magnetization reversal in the sub-20 nm MTJs.
